Revise rather than accept because the implementation contradicts its own mechanism on wave64 SIMD: guarding the reciprocal with if (iqs==0) makes lanes 0 and 32 compute while the other 62 lanes idle under the exec mask, costing exactly the same wall time as letting all lanes compute the value (amax is already segment-uniform after warp_reduce_max). The lane-0 specialization therefore saves nothing, and the added __shfl_sync broadcast is a real inserted cost on the critical path (ds_bpermute LDS round-trip on gfx90a) plus branch/exec-mask overhead. At ikv=1 (iq=7) the output pointer lands 7 full planes past the allocation — out-of-bounds writes on every required GQA7 correctness case (nh=2, nr23=[7,1] gives K->ne[2]=2, so ikv=1 is always reached). The stated falsifier "Dedicated correctness fails any GQA7 shape" fires deterministically. Correct slicing must use dst->nb[1]/ne[1] (as the patch already does correctly for sinks). Additionally, dst_main retains ne[1]=14 while Q_main.ne[2]=6, risking a head-count consistency assert in launch_fattn. (2) Dispatch cannot match the sealed candidate variants: the template's controller-derived cells (derived_from_anchor_by_exact_7_equals_3x2_plus_1_partition) declare one bulk launch (flash_attn_tile<64,64,1,2,false>, grid 3072, 3096 calls) and one tail launch (flash_attn_tile<64,64,2,1,false>, grid 1024, 3096 calls) per op, i.e., a single launch pair covering all 6 head-pairs and both tail heads. Because bulk heads {0-5, 7-12} are non-uniformly strided, host-side pointer slicing forces the per-KV-group loop, producing 2 bulk + 2 tail launches per op (6192 calls each at roughly half grids, ~1536/512). This violates the hypothesis stop rule "Stop if paired-head dispatch is not exact" and the sealed variant identity. This removes the second global-memory read of the row after the block_reduce barrier (which otherwise forces a reload, since values cannot be kept live across __syncthreads by the compiler). It is a load-reduction change with unchanged arithmetic and unchanged launch geometry, which is precisely what the falsifier requires; it does not touch wave count, so it does not match dnr-rms-two-wave (launch_geometry, four-to-two waves) or any other DNR fingerprint.

The second-pass register selection maps col in [k*256,(k+1)*256) to xk correctly, and threads whose guarded loads were skipped never enter the corresponding loop iterations. All other instantiations (block_size 1024, do_add variants, plain rms) fall through to the unchanged generic path via if constexpr, keeping blast radius minimal.

One residual risk, contained: the specialization implicitly assumes ncols <= 4*block_size = 1024 for the <256,true,false> instantiation; there is no in-kernel guard, so a hypothetical launch of this instantiation with ncols >= 1024 would silently drop columns.
